title: Fixed-Modulo Latency Sampling Aliasing with Periodic Work
pattern: Latency is sampled on a fixed deterministic period (every Nth request, every Nth tick) with no randomization.
why_bad: Systems do periodic work (buffer flushes, batch commits, key rotation, GC) every so many requests or milliseconds. A fixed sampling period can lock onto that cycle and systematically hit or miss the stalls (aliasing), so sampled percentiles are biased in an unknown direction.
detection: Latency or timing measurement guarded by `count % CONSTANT == 0` (or an equivalent fixed-stride condition) with no random offset, jitter or probabilistic sampling.
counterexample: Probabilistic sampling (`rng.gen::<f64>() < rate`), reservoir sampling, Poisson-timed sampling, or instrumentation that records every request.
source: Richard L. Sites, *Understanding Software Dynamics* (2021), Ch. 12, p. 202.
